conventions.convention: The mechanical presentation uses N≥1 labels with positive masses, an open Cartesian configuration domain Q, a C2 potential U and separately declared residual forces d. Cartesian momentum is p=Mv; for a time-independent C3 immersion X, generalized momentum is p=G(q)v with G=DXᵀM DX.

Velocity regularity means a nonsingular velocity Hessian. A local inverse branch means a C1 inverse between open neighbourhoods of full time-configuration-velocity and time-configuration-momentum states.

Hyperregularity requires each velocity fibre map to be a bijection onto the entire momentum fibre, with a jointly C1 inverse assignment on the whole phase chart; it does not assert completeness of dynamics.

H=p·v−L is evaluated at the inverse Legendre velocity. Its dimension is energy; generalized momentum component p_a has dimension action divided by the coordinate dimension. Changing U to U+c(t), while retaining the required regularity, changes H to H+c(t).

Unforced Hamilton equations and stationary-action curves describe model motions on the branch d≡0. For general residual forces, d or its pullback Qres is added to the momentum equation. Constraint elimination additionally assumes a scleronomic regular holonomic datum and ideal reactions.

H equals mechanical energy along arbitrary C2 curves in inertial Cartesian coordinates and time-independent generalized coordinates. The stated conservation condition requires a time-independent potential representative and zero residual force.

The pendulum angle is dimensionless and represented modulo 2π. Two real angular charts cover the circle; overlap transitions add a constant multiple of 2π and leave momentum unchanged. Its constraint is bilateral with the ideal-reaction law.
The exponential Lagrangian e^v is a purely mathematical chart example. Its inverse and Hamiltonian are defined only for p>0, with no physical units or mechanical-model interpretation asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For the adopted potential presentation and every declared generalized-coordinate map X, the Cartesian and generalized fibre maps are bijections with C2 inverses v=M⁻¹p and v=G(q)⁻¹p. Their C2 Hamiltonians are H=½p·M⁻¹p+U and H̃=½p·G(q)⁻¹p+Ũ.

On a nonempty open interval, for C2 curves with their mechanical momentum, model motion, Hamilton equations and stationarity on every closed subinterval are equivalent when d≡0. With residual forces, the corresponding forced equations are equivalent. Declared generalized-coordinate Lagrange equations are equivalent to their Hamilton system; with the additional zero-residual, scleronomic regular constraint and ideal-reaction hypotheses, these describe the induced constrained motion.

The momentum of a Cartesian state is p=Mv, identified with the velocity fibre derivative of L=K−U. For a declared generalized-coordinate map, the generalized momentum is p=L̃_v=G(q)v, with its stated covector pairing and component dimensions.
For a hyperregular presentation with inverse Legendre branch v, define H(t,x,p)=p·v(t,x,p)−L(t,x,v(t,x,p)); the generalized-coordinate Hamiltonian is the same construction for L̃.

The Cartesian branch Hamiltonian equals K+U along every C2 curve with p=Mx′. Along a model motion its derivative is ∂tU plus residual-force power, and it is constant if ∂tU≡0 and d≡0. The same energy identity holds for induced curves in time-independent generalized coordinates.
The velocity Hessians are M and G(q), both symmetric positive definite, so both mechanical charts are regular at every state and admit local C1 inverse Legendre branches there.

concerns.concern: Verification 1.3 says “differentiating the identity e^{v(p)}=p by the chain rule gives” v′(p)=1/p, but F3 supplies only bijectivity and no prior step establishes differentiability of the inverse. The local-inverse result already cited in F1 can supply that differentiability; uniqueness then identifies its local branches with v(p)=ln p. The calculation is correct once this short prerequisite argument is stated.

The final Remarks paragraph calls H “the conserved quantity H of [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-branch-identities]] clause 3” along solutions of Hamilton's equations without the supplier's condition that L_t vanish along the trajectory. Clause 3 instead states e′=−L_t. For the admissible presentation U(t,x)=at with nonzero constant a of power dimension and d=0, the force vanishes, straight-line motions satisfy Hamilton's equations, and H′=a≠0. The theorem's numbered statement is correctly qualified, but this remark makes a false unconditional conservation claim.

Definition (d) says “when more than one branch exists it is part of the data, as in [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]”. The cited hyperregularity definition requires fibre bijectivity, so its global inverse branch is unique. Multiple local inverse choices concern a different, merely regular setting and should not be attributed to this hyperregular definition.

alerts.finding: Definition (c) writes “the state curve z=(x,ẋ):J→D” and later “z(t)∈D”, while (a) defines D=I0×Q×R^{3N}. The pair (x,ẋ) has 6N components and belongs to Q×R^{3N}; the triple (t,x,ẋ) belongs to D. The stated equivalence therefore contains a state/time-state type mismatch, although the component equations convey the intended equivalence.

F2 says “the model's motions with p=Mx′ are exactly the solutions of Hamilton's equations of H” under the general presentation (U,d), without the d≡0 qualification of pthm-cm12-hamilton-equivalence clause 1. For nonzero residual force the momentum equation has an additional d term. This item's numbered clauses and proof 1.2 correctly distinguish the potential branch, but F2 restates its supplier too strongly.

The introductory Definition paragraph says “motions of the model are the integral curves of the branch Hamiltonian field, in each chart with its own Hamiltonian” after adopting a general presentation (U,d). The cited CM13 theorem requires d≡0 for the unforced identification; residual forces require the forced field. Clause (b) later includes “on the potential branch”, but the introductory supplier restatement omits that restriction.

L1 says “the map x↦Mx′=mx′ is the inverse Legendre branch”. In CM12 the velocity-to-momentum map is v↦Mv; the inverse Legendre branch is p↦M⁻¹p=p/m. The displayed expression describes momentum along a curve and reverses the direction of the cited inverse branch. The example's Hamiltonian formula remains correct.

seams_checked.note: Mechanical L=K−U, static C3 immersions, potential-branch stationarity and ideal scleronomic constraint reduction retain their supplier hypotheses.
The potential representative, residual-force split and energy balance are faithfully imported. The independent overstatement in the energy item's final remark is recorded in concerns.
Uses the adopted force equation and motion notion without asserting completeness. The external definition's state/time-state type mismatch is separately alerted.

Local/global Legendre and branch identities are used correctly in the numbered proofs, but pthm-cm12-energy-time's final remark drops the vanishing-L_t condition from the cited branch-energy conservation statement.
Positive labelled masses, the block mass operator, inertial coordinates and dimension conventions are preserved.
Constraint claims retain regularity, scleronomy and the adopted ideal-reaction condition; no unrestricted phase-space constraint theory is inferred.

The polynomial gauge function meets the full-domain C3 requirement; the moving-coordinate substitution has invertible spatial derivative; pendulum reduction is applied on restricted ambient chart domains.
The moving spring correctly has E′=−kv0y1, while its substituted Hamiltonian differs by v0p′1. Potential and energy representatives remain explicit.
The explicit uniform-field and free motions meet the standing force hypotheses; their all-real-time solutions justify the claimed maximality.
Mass, length, time, force, momentum and action dimensions are consistent, including angular momentum coordinates and the gauge parameter.
The pendulum constraint has rank two on its circle and uses bilateral ideal reactions; the prescribed moving support is correctly treated as external potential data rather than a constraint reaction.

Generic chart hyperregularity handles affine momentum shifts and moving coordinates. The exponential example computes its image-restricted branch locally rather than asserting the global proposition's hypotheses; its omitted inverse-differentiability argument is recorded.

Momentum and Hamiltonian formulas agree, and the main field-equivalence clauses retain residual-force qualifications. However, pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations F2 omits d≡0 in its unforced model-motion restatement.
Free, oscillator and Verlet examples explicitly use zero residual force; the full-dimensional point transformation correctly converts generalized momentum by DX⁻ᵀ.

Hamilton–Jacobi characteristics distinguish Cartesian model motions from generalized-coordinate Lagrange solutions and impose d≡0 for their model reading. The introductory model-reading sentence in def-cm14-involution omits that qualification.
The explicit mechanical Hamiltonians agree with CM12, but ex-cm14-harmonic-oscillator-hamilton-jacobi-check L1 incorrectly names momentum mx′ as the inverse Legendre branch.
